topic: Learning to Belong to Yourself
script:
You're tracing the cracks in your bedroom ceiling.
A spider weaves her world above you,
steady,
patient.
She doesn't ask the walls to change shape.
The corners know her name.
You press your palm to the cool glass,
watch your breath fog the night.
It doesn't stay,
but it was yours for a moment.
The streetlight hums a lullaby.
You hum back,
quietly,
until the melody belongs to you.

topic: The Way You Look When You Do Not Know I Am Watching
script:
The way your fingers trace the rim,
of an empty glass,
like you’re reading braille off yesterday’s news.
Somewhere between hunger,
and forgetting you haven’t eaten.
Your shadow stretches,
longer than the afternoon,
but refuses to let go of the chair.
I count the cracks in the ceiling,
while you count the steps,
to a door that isn’t there.
And when the light shifts,
you don’t flinch,
just tilt your head,
like the world owes you an answer.

topic: What I Mean When I Say I Love You
script:
You trace the cracks in the ceiling.
Like constellations only we know,
I memorize the way your fingers hesitate.
Not afraid,
just savoring the weight of what comes next.
Your laugh is a pocket of air in stale rooms,
something small I carry between my ribs.
I don’t mean forever,
I mean this breath,
this quiet click of the lamp turning off,
your shoulder against mine like a question I don’t answer.
Stay. Just like this.
send this to them.

topic: When You Love Someone Who Is Leaving
script:
I still pack their favorite sweater
in the suitcase every trip
just in case the road brings them home again
The zipper sticks at the same corner
a memory I can’t force shut
Some nights I leave it open
like an invitation
but the wind only carries dust
not their voice
I won’t close it completely
not yet
let the moths decide.

topic: Being Misunderstood
script:
The last text you sent was still unsent.
It flickers like a moth against the screen,
soft wings brushing glass.
They read it three times,
but never saw the way your fingers trembled
while typing each letter.
WORDS don't always land where we aim.
Sometimes they scatter like seeds in the wind,
and grow into something wild,
something unrecognizable.
You keep the draft,
quiet proof of a truth they'll never understand.
send this to them.

topic: Falling For Someone Who Does Not Know
script:
Tuesday, 2:17pm. The café hums.
Your name slips through my lips,
just a breath,
like sugar dissolving in tea.
I stir too long,
watching the swirl,
not tasting,
just waiting for the sweetness to settle.
Some words,
I write them down,
then tear the page,
not from anger,
but from knowing,
the ink was never yours to keep.

topic: The Cost Of Always Being Available
script:
You're not tired. Just spent.
We answer every call.
We make ourselves reachable.
It feels kind. Like being a reliable friend.
But they stop looking for you.
They just know you're there.
Always.
And you taught them.
That your effort has no real cost.

topic: The Night You Stopped Waiting
script:
YOU LEFT THE LIGHT ON
in the kitchen
again
like I’d walk through that door
any second
I stopped checking the clock
stopped setting two plates
stopped pretending the couch
wasn’t just mine now
SOMEWHERE
between the last text
and the first gray hair
you became
a name I don’t say out loud
anymore

topic: What Home Actually Feels Like
script:
Home isn’t walls. Not really.
It’s the way the kettle hums,
just before it boils,
warm and patient,
like someone who knows you’re coming.
The sink is full of dishes,
but the water runs clear,
and for once,
you don’t mind the weight.
Some rooms remember your shape,
even when you forget.
You leave,
but the door never locks behind you.
It just waits.

topic: The Gift of Impermanence
script:
There's a quiet like dandelion seeds.
They land,
soft,
on your palm.
You know they won't stay,
but you cup them anyway.
The wind takes them,
not cruel,
just honest.
Some things are meant to be held,
then let go.
The gift isn't the keeping.
It's the moment you chose to open your hands.
send this to them.

topic: The Person Behind My Smile
script:
There's a quiet like a held breath
before the laugh escapes.
The way your fingers trace the rim of a cup,
unaware I'm memorizing the shape of your pause.
I built this smile from old receipts,
ink fading with every thank you,
and the corners curl when no one's looking.
Your name fits in the spaces between my teeth
where I hide the words I won't say out loud.
The clock hums,
but time moves differently near you—
slower,
softer,
like snow settling on a windowsill.
I let you see the version that knows how to glow,
while the real me
counts the cracks in the ceiling.
send this to them.

topic: Silent Suffering Nobody Sees
script:
The old gardener whispered
some wounds
never break the skin.
They bloom inward
like roots in the dark.

You walk through rooms
carrying a weight
no one names.
The body remembers
what the mouth won’t say.

Let the ache
rest like a stone
in your pocket.

topic: The Difference Between Living and Existing
script:
An old gardener whispered
roots don’t ask for light
they reach anyway
toward what they need
without knowing why.

I think that’s living —
not the bloom
the stubborn underground stretch
when no one’s watching.
Existing is just waiting
for the rain to stop.
Maybe the dirt
is enough.

topic: When You Miss Someone You Should Not
script:
I stopped counting the hours,
they pool like rainwater in my shoes.
Every puddle reflects your shadow,
but the sidewalk stays empty.
I trace your initials on fogged glass,
the letters disappear before I finish.
Some days,
the ache feels like a borrowed coat,
too big,
too heavy,
I wear it anyway.
The radiator hums your favorite song,
I pretend it's you humming back.
Send this to them.

topic: The Last Text You Never Sent
script:
The cursor blinked
once
then twice
like a streetlight about to die.
I typed your name
and the whole screen
held its breath.
YOU WERE GONE
before the first word
landed.
Still,
I saved it
like a ticket stub
to a show
that never opened.

topic: When Love Feels Like Coming Home
script:
I stopped counting the steps
to your door.
The porch light hums,
soft orange like the last sip of tea.
I never told you how the floorboards creak
in the same rhythm as my old clock,
ticking your name.
Your voice,
a blanket draped over my shoulders
before I knew I was cold.
The way you leave the window open
just enough for the breeze to visit.
I carry it everywhere,
this quiet shape of belonging.
send this to them.

topic: The Power of Small Moments
script:
There's a kind of wonder that fits in your palm.
A single raindrop on the window,
holding the whole sky inside.
It doesn't ask to be noticed,
just lingers,
and the world feels softer for it.
Your laugh does that too—
unfolds like a paper crane,
small,
but suddenly the room is lighter.
I keep these moments in my pockets,
where they warm my hands.
Send this to them.

topic: The Way You Look When You Do Not Know I Am Watching
script:
You're folding laundry like it's sacred,
just the way your mother taught you.
The sleeves align,
perfect creases,
but your eyes drift
to the window where the streetlight hums.
Some nights,
you let the wrinkles stay,
and I see the weight you carry
when no one's looking.
You smooth the collar,
slowly,
like you're tucking in a memory.
I won't interrupt.

topic: The Moment You Stopped Hoping
script:
You’re staring at the ceiling again.
The cracks don’t spell anything anymore,
just lines you’ve memorized.
Somewhere,
a clock ticks,
but it’s not counting down to anything.
The hands that once reached,
now rest,
weightless,
like balloons untied.
You don’t flinch when the phone buzzes,
not even a blink.
The moment hope left,
it didn’t slam the door,
just clicked the latch.
and you let it go.

topic: Falling For Someone Who Does Not Know
script:
The porch light stays on all night.
just for you,
though you’ll never walk up the steps.
I trace your name
in the condensation on my window,
but the glass forgets by morning.
Some nights,
I swear I hear your laugh
in the static between radio stations.
The universe keeps sending signals,
and I keep pretending not to notice.
This is how ghosts are made.
quietly.

topic: Staying Too Long
script:
The porch light still flickers at 3 a.m.
not for safety
just habit
Some nights I sit there
watching the moths circle the bulb
and wonder if they ever tire of orbiting
The key still fits the lock
but the door creaks louder now
like it’s warning me
I could leave the key on the table
walk away
but the moths don’t know how to stop.

topic: The Person Behind My Smile
script:
How do you tell someone
about the weight
that lives behind your teeth,
not sadness,
just the quiet hum
of a radio tuned to static,
Some days it’s louder,
others it fades
but the dial never moves,
The smile isn’t a lie,
just the volume turned down,
so the world can hear
the song I pretend to sing.

topic: Silent Suffering Nobody Sees
script:
4:17 a.m. The fridge hums alone.
It’s not hunger,
just the sound of something breathing.
The bruises on your ribs
are pressed into the mattress,
not from fists,
from carrying what you can’t name.
Some nights,
the weight doesn’t even wake you.
It just sits,
a guest who never leaves,
and you learn to sleep through the ache.
The house won’t tell.

topic: Friends Who Only Call When They Need You
script:
Friday night. The fridge hums low.
Your name lights up the screen,
not with hello,
just a question mark,
soft as a door left ajar.
The hands that once passed you a drink
now only pass you the weight,
the same old script,
the same old need.
I answer,
not out of kindness,
but the ghost of a habit.
Let them go.

topic: The One I Think About First
script:
How do you name the person
who lives in the first light of morning?
Not the sunrise,
but the thought
before your eyes open.
Some memories
are like a favorite sweater—
not worn,
just kept close enough to touch.
The one I reach for
when the room is too quiet,
too full,
too anything.
I don’t call,
I don’t text,
I just let the weight of them
settle like dust on my shoulders.
Let them know.

topic: The Part You Never Talk About
script:
The way you laugh
when the story’s too old to tell
but you tell it anyway.

WE ALL KNOW
it’s not funny anymore
just familiar.

Your hands
still shape the air
like they did back then
when the words mattered.

NOW THEY DON’T
but you keep talking
and I keep listening
for the part you never say.

topic: When Being Nice Made You A Target
script:
Generosity is often misread.
Some people interpret kindness,
as availability.
They see your open hand,
not your worth.
They assume your grace means,
you have no edge.
No line to cross.
You teach people how to take from you,
by how much you let them.

topic: The Power of Small Moments
script:
The way you laughed
before you knew
I was listening
stuck in my ribs
like a loose button
I never sewed back.
YOU KEPT IT
in a drawer with ticket stubs
and that one sock
no one ever claimed.
Now it rattles
when the wind blows just right
through the screen door.

topic: When You Realized You Were the Option, Not the Priority
script:
YOU WERE THE EXTRA
key on the ring
I carried loose
in my pocket
clinking against the one
that actually started the car.
I never lost you
just stopped reaching
for the jingle
that didn’t matter.
Somewhere between then and now
you became the station
I only scan
when static fills the drive.

topic: When You Found Me
script:
the desert wind whispered
when you found me
i was not lost
just waiting
for the shape of your shadow to stretch across mine.

years of dust had settled
yet my edges stayed sharp
like stones the river forgot to smooth.

you didn’t carry a lantern
or call my name
you simply walked
until the space between us
became a place.

topic: The Beauty of an Unfinished Life
script:
The way the morning light
lingers
on your unmade bed
like it knows
something you don’t.
You leave the door ajar
not for the breeze
but for the stories
that haven’t arrived yet.
THE SUNSET STILL WAITS
for your shadow to stretch
just a little longer.
you let it.

topic: You Are My Calm
script:
There's a stillness that hums,
like a fridge in an empty kitchen.
You are the steady buzz,
the one I lean against
when the world spins too loud.
I don't need you to fix it,
just stand there,
quiet as a held breath,
and let the noise
pass through me like wind.
You are my calm,
not the absence of storm,
but the hand I reach for in the dark.

topic: Why Peace Is Not the Absence of Storm
script:
The porch swing still creaks at midnight.
Not from wind,
just the weight of what we carried.
Some storms don’t roar,
they settle in the joints of old wood,
warping the grain,
but never breaking it.
The quiet after isn’t peace,
just the shape of us,
holding what we survived.
You’ll recognize it,
when the ache feels like home.

topic: The Smile That Hides Everything
script:
It’s not a smile. It’s a pocket.
You tuck the whole sky inside it,
folding edges neatly.
No one sees the storm you carry,
just the quiet gold of your teeth.
But sometimes,
the stitches unravel,
and the stars spill out like loose change.
I pick them up,
press them back into your palm.
Keep the night safe for me.
send this to them.

topic: What I Mean When I Say I Love You
script:
We forget how heavy light can be.
The way it lingers
on the edges of your shadow,
not fading,
just waiting for you to turn around.
Some promises don’t need words,
they hum in the quiet hum of the fridge,
in the way your keys still jingle
like they did the first time.
I won’t ask you to stay,
but I’ll leave the porch light on,
just in case you’re passing through.
Let them know.

topic: Finding Yourself After Them
script:
You're tracing the cracks in the ceiling again.
The same ones you memorized,
but now they look like rivers.
Not maps,
just paths you didn't choose.
Your fingers remember their shape,
and slowly,
the weight of their name
feels lighter than the dust
settling on your windowsill.
Some mornings,
you wake up and forget to miss them.
The sun spills in,
uninvited,
and you let it stay.

topic: Being Tired in Ways Sleep Cannot Fix
script:
You’re peeling an orange at midnight.
The rind spirals down like a tired question.
No one answers.
Slowly the segments split,
too bright,
too much effort.
You press one to your tongue,
but the sweetness
can’t dissolve the weight
in your shoulders.
The juice drips.
Send this to them.

topic: The People Who Disappear When It's Hard
script:
Commitment is not measured in laughter.
Or shared memory.
We confuse good times.
With deep roots.
Then everything shifts.
The ground gets unsteady.
And the hands you thought were holding yours.
Are gone.
They just let go.
Quietly.
They were never really holding on.

topic: What I Never Said Out Loud
script:
The clock hands never asked for my secrets.
I fed them anyway,
tiny crumbs of truth
swallowed by the gears.
Some nights,
the ticking grows teeth,
chews through the dark
like a moth through wool.
I let it.
The holes are where the light gets in,
but the light doesn’t know my name.

topic: Loving Without Losing Yourself
script:
You held the door,
I
let the wind
carry my name out first.
It didn’t mind,
just curled around your ankles
like a cat who chose you,
but still sleeps on my side.
SOMEHOW
we built a life
without moving the furniture,
and when the light slants just so,
I forget
which shadow is yours.

topic: The First Heartbreak
script:
The first heartbreak isn’t about them leaving.
It’s the way your own hands
start to feel like strangers,
buttoning shirts you’ll never wear for them,
folding sleeves that no longer reach.
Some mornings,
you catch your reflection mid-wave,
mid-smile,
and the mirror flinches first.
Not from pain,
from recognition—
that version of you
is already packed away.

topic: When You Love Someone Who Is Leaving
script:
How do you name the ache
when the suitcase is still open
but the room already echoes?
Not goodbye,
just the shape of air
after they step through.
The door doesn’t slam,
just sighs,
settles into its frame
like a tired shoulder.
Some part of you stays unpacked,
waiting for the weight to shift back.
Let them go.

topic: The Quiet Exit
script:
The last text never gets sent.
It sits in drafts,
like a boat
that missed the tide.
Some exits don’t slam,
they dissolve—
the way sugar
vanishes in tea.
Your name stays sweet,
but the aftertaste
fades to nothing.
I won’t wave goodbye.
Just let the current take me.

topic: The Quiet Revolution of Self-Respect
script:
a japanese gardener whispered
not every root needs light
some grow strongest
where the soil stays dark
trust the unseen work
self-respect isn't a shout
it's the quiet refusal
to let others dig up your peace
you don't need their tools
or their permission to thrive
some things grow best
in the hush of your own hands

topic: Grieving Someone Who Did Not Die
script:
I keep your old voicemail
saved
like a secret
no one else knows.
The way you laughed
still tangled in the wires,
static humming your name.
I press play
when the house is too empty,
but the voice that answers
isn’t yours anymore.
Just a ghost
in the shape of hello.

topic: When Just Being Near You Is Enough
script:
You don’t need words. Not here.
The air hums low between us,
like a radio left on in another room.
I count the freckles on your shoulder,
each one a tiny constellation I’ve memorized.
Sometimes,
your breath syncs with mine
without either of us trying.
It’s not magic.
Just physics.
The way gravity pulls without asking.
I could stay like this forever.
send this to them.

topic: When Someone Chooses You Every Day
script:
Choosing is louder than saying yes once.
The morning light still lands,
just on your side of the bed.
Not grand gestures,
just the way you reach,
when the coffee’s too hot.
Some decisions aren’t spoken,
they’re the quiet weight of a hand,
resting where yours has always been.
And the world keeps asking why,
but the answer’s in the way,
you turn the key,
every single day.

topic: The Strength in Stillness
script:
You held the door for the storm
and it
stayed.
Bare feet on wet wood
counting the seconds between thunder
until the house learned to breathe again.
WE WERE NEVER AFRAID
we were just
waiting
for the right kind of quiet
to teach us how to stand
inside the weight of it
without breaking.

topic: The Way You Look at Me
script:
It’s not a look. It’s a slow dissolve.
The room tilts,
just enough to notice.
Your eyes don’t hold mine—
they unravel the seams,
thread by careful thread.
I forget how to stand.
The floor remembers your name,
but my knees don’t.
You blink,
and the world rewrites itself.
Send this to them.

topic: Lying Awake Replaying Everything
script:
The night replays like a stuck record.
Needle skips,
but the song never changes.
Every word,
every pause,
carved deeper into the vinyl.
Some grooves you can’t smooth out,
just learn to live inside.
The static hums,
and I wonder
if anyone else hears it.
The silence isn’t empty.
It’s full of echoes.
Send this to them.

topic: The Text You Read But Did Not Reply To
script:
There's a quiet like the space between raindrops,
still holding the shape of what fell.
The screen glows,
letters sharp as thorns you can't unsee.
Your fingers hover,
but the cursor blinks like a held breath.
It's not hesitation,
just the weight of words already spoken in silence.
The message stays,
soft as a footprint in new snow.
You trace the edges,
but never press send.
There's no reply,
only the echo of your own name.

topic: Why Peace Is Not the Absence of Storm
script:
Remember the last time you smelled
burnt toast.
That sharp tang
before the smoke alarm screamed.
You didn’t know it yet
but the day was already different.

Peace isn’t the kitchen quiet again.
It’s the way you stirred the jam
one last time
before the jar disappeared from the fridge.

You still reach for it sometimes.

topic: The Strength In Walking Away
script:
When did it become easier to stay
than to leave quietly?

We call it loyalty.
They call it convenience.

You memorize the cracks in their voice,
the exact shade of their bad moods,
the way they say your name like a question.

You think walking away is the coward’s move.
But staying when you’ve already checked out?
That’s the real performance.

The strongest people aren’t the ones who endure.
They’re the ones who know when to stop.

topic: The Version of You That Did Not Make It
script:
I carry it everywhere.
A pocket-sized constellation,
wrapped in receipts and lint.
No one sees the way it glows,
soft as a streetlamp through fog.
You left it behind,
that version of you,
the one who laughed at bad jokes.
I press it to my ear sometimes,
but the static just hums your name.
Maybe it’s not a star after all.
Maybe it’s a door,
left slightly ajar.

topic: When Love Was Not Enough
script:
YOU KEPT THE LIGHTS ON
all night
so the dark wouldn’t notice
we were failing.

I traced your veins
like subway lines
to places we’d never go again.

The couch still holds
our old shape
like a photograph
you can sit inside.

We ran out of words
before we ran out of time
and that’s the part
no one warns you about.

topic: Being Strong for Everyone While Breaking Inside
script:
You’re stitching the seams of your sleeves again.
Needle pricks,
but the thread never snaps.
They see the embroidery,
the tiny flowers you add,
not the holes you’re hiding.
Your hands know the weight of holding,
steady for everyone,
while your ribs learn to bend.
The fabric stretches,
but doesn’t tear.
You fold the shirt neatly.
Place it back on the hanger.

topic: The Friends Who Only Stayed For The Good Days
script:
You thought loyalty was a two-way street.
It wasn’t.
Some friends only show up for the view,
not the climb.
You carried the snacks,
they carried the stories.
You remember the laughter,
but who remembers the blisters?
They’ll call you dramatic
when you finally stop answering.
The truth?
You weren’t the problem.
You were just the only one who stayed.

topic: What Home Actually Feels Like
script:
Home isn’t a place you find.
It’s the echo of spoons,
clinking in a kitchen drawer at 3 a.m.,
when the world’s asleep
but the fridge hums a lullaby.
Somewhere,
a door left ajar,
just enough to let the cat slip through,
and the scent of rain on pavement
lingers like a promise.
The walls don’t hold it—
the air does,
thick with the weight of small, ordinary things.

topic: When You Cry in the Car Alone
script:
Midnight. The engine hums like a lullaby.
You’re not lost,
just circling the same empty block,
windows fogged with ghosts of what could’ve been.
The steering wheel knows your grip,
knuckles white as the moon outside,
but the road doesn’t ask questions.
Some tears aren’t for sadness,
they’re for the version of you
who believed in answers.
The car keeps moving.
You don’t have to.

topic: The First Heartbreak
script:
You’re peeling the label off your water bottle,
again.
The glue sticks to your fingers like old promises,
stubborn.
You tell yourself it’s just habit,
not hunger,
not the way your ribs remember their shape.
Some nights,
the bed feels like a raft
adrift,
and you’re the only one who notices the tide.
You count the cracks in the ceiling,
but the numbers keep changing.
The first heartbreak isn’t a wound,
it’s a shadow
learning to walk without you.
